title: KVCache TTL shadow leakage: detection signals and staged sanitization
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Production hosts experienced gradual heap growth and eviction storms over a 72h window on 2026-03-08 -> 2026-03-10 that led to degraded serving latency and a small number of OOM restarts. Root cause analysis indicates a race between async TTL-refresh, prefetch paths, and compaction that allowed shadow/ghost entries to persist in the prefix->KV mapping. These shadow entries retained large value buffers (embeddings, long context segments) preventing reclamation. The incident surface: increased GC/compaction time, eviction backpressure, tenant tail latencies increased, and memory fragmentation. This ticket tracks follow-ups: detection signals, staged mitigations already deployed, long-term code fixes, and runbook + test improvements.
updates: 2026-03-10: Initial pagerduty alert — several serving hosts in us-west-2 showed >85% RSS growth over 6 hours. Emergency action: disabled aggressive prefetch for top-10 suspect tenants; turned on eviction-throttle configuration. (Pagerduty incident: PD-66912)

2026-03-11: Heap profiles and core dumps analyzed. Noticed stable live pointer counts tied to prefix index entries; values referenced by epoch pointers not reclaimed after compaction. Reproducer created locally via eviction storm harness. Assigned to Marco for mitigation and Aisha for telemetry.

2026-03-12: Hotfix deployed (runtime: enable-ttl-sweep) which increases compaction frequency and forces pointer reconciliation during async compaction. Immediate memory growth stopped on canary fleet. No increased error rate observed. Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5123

2026-03-13: We validated canary for 24h. Memory profiles show reclaimed >92% of previously leaked buffers. Still seeing intermittent small shadow counts during micro-benchmarks — delaying full rollout until permanent invariant is in place. This ticket created to track permanent fixes and observability additions.

acceptance_criteria: Memory leak (heap growth) is not reproducible with eviction-storm harness across 24h run on staging with production-like load
No increase in tail latencies or OOM events during canary rollout for 48h at target traffic levels
New metrics available in Console: prefix_shadow_entries, slab_occupancy_ratio, tenant_live_entry_count; alerts configured and tested
Unit/fuzz tests covering the race condition are added and stable in CI
Runbook updated with step-by-step mitigation and verified by SRE run through
resources: Incident timeline and pager logs: https://incidents.redwood.ai/PD-66912
runbook_changes: Added emergency toggles (disable-prefetch, enable-ttl-sweep, enable-eviction-throttle) and a checklist for safe canary ramp. Document contains play-by-play commands, expected signals, and post-fix verification steps.
notes: This incident highlighted an under-tested combinatorial race between prefetch and compaction. Longer term we should evaluate redesigning prefetch to avoid holding epoch pointers across async boundaries, and consider bounded-prefetch sized by tenant memory budget. Also consider moving heavy-value buffers to off-heap arenas that are explicitly reference-counted and recyclers with deterministic free paths.
